hook_text: Two hundred and fifty years ago, a spoon of sugar in a cup of tea in London had a hidden price.
clip_script: That sugar came from a plantation in the Caribbean. To grow it, enslaved Africans cut cane in burning heat and worked crushing mills and boiling houses day and night at harvest. So many died that planters simply bought more people. Why use enslaved workers? Profit. No wages. Laws said enslaved people were property, and racist lies were invented to excuse it. Ships sailed a triangle: guns and cloth from Europe to Africa, captives across the Atlantic, then sugar, tobacco and cotton back to Europe. The cotton fed English factories. Port cities grew rich. Banks grew rich. The people whose labour made it all received nothing. Next time you hear about the Industrial Revolution, remember who paid for it.
visual_style: A whiteboard teacup with a sugar cube; the camera pulls back to a ship, a plantation, a mill; three arrows form a triangle between Europe, Africa and the Americas; coins piling up in Europe.
pacing: Everyday hook, a widening chain of cause and effect, a pointed close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and follow the money of the slave trade.
